question: When examining charred remains to determine whether burns were ante-mortem or post-mortem, the most reliable histological indicator of a vital reaction is:

answers.text: The presence of cherry-red discolouration of the skin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Cherry-red discolouration is a sign of carbon monoxide poisoning and does not by itself confirm ante-mortem burning.

answers.text: Polymorphonuclear (PMN) leucocyte infiltration at the burn margins

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. PMN infiltration at burn margins is the histological hallmark of vital reaction — it confirms the individual was alive when the burn was sustained. Other signs (serum blisters, hyperaemia) are supportive but PMN infiltration is the most reliable.

answers.text: The pugilistic (boxer's) attitude of the burned body

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The pugilistic attitude results from heat-induced muscle protein coagulation and contraction — it occurs in both ante-mortem and post-mortem burns and does NOT indicate vital reaction.

answers.text: The depth of the burn (third-degree or full-thickness burns only)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Burn depth does not determine vitality; ante-mortem burns can be any depth, and the same is true for post-mortem burns.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key vital reaction signs in burns: hyperaemia, serum blisters, and — most reliably — PMN leucocyte infiltration at margins. The pugilistic attitude is a heat artefact and does NOT indicate the person was alive.
Correct. PMN infiltration is the key histological vital reaction sign. Remember: pugilistic attitude is NOT a vital reaction.
